news.title: UEFA "Recall World Cup Boycott"... Yet 'FIFA President Must Resign' Backlash Continues
news.lede: The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA) appears to have forgiven FIFA to some extent. UEFA, which had declared a boycott of FIFA-organized tournaments in protest against FIFA President Gianni Infantino's push to sell stakes in the World Cup through private equity funds, has now decided to withdraw the boycott. British outlet 'BBC' reported on the 26th (Korean time) that "UEFA plans to withdraw its threat of boycotting FIFA-organized tournaments after receiving assurances that In Pan-ti-no (Chairman)'s plan to sell World Cup stakes to private investors will not be repeated." On the same day, FIFA also expressed its welcome, stating, "We are pleased that all teams qualifying for the upcoming Under-20 (U-20) Women's World Cup will participate."

news.title: UEFA set to withdraw FIFA boycott threat ahead of Champions League draw
news.lede: Thursday's draw for this season's Champions League has been somewhat overshadowed by the latest developments in the dispute between UEFA and FIFA over plans to bring private financing into the World Cup, with European football's governing body expected to drop a threatened boycott of global competitions. UEFA, whose clubs and national teams dominate football's global economy, reacted furiously when it emerged in late July that Gianni Infantino's FIFA was aiming to create a commercial subsidiary to run its biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup. The proposal would have allowed private investors to acquire stakes in a company created under the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative. UEFA, under president Aleksander Ceferin, had described the proposal in scathing terms, labelling it a "shady, opaque backroom deal".

news.title: Uefa to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
news.lede: Uefa has received guarantees after ill-fated Infantino plan. European sides will go to under-20 Women’s World Cup. Uefa is to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. European teams have been cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.
